messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: fixed lgamma-based crashes (from neg_binomial)
parts:
The problem was that an exception was being thrown
during the lgamma_vari constructor by Boost's lgamma
implementation. Daniel and I pulled the lgamma
calc out of the constructor, and now everything works
fine.

That negative binomial model doesn't crash any
more, but the model itself still doesn't work.

But I think that's just HMC, not a bug. We should
probably build some example negative binomial models
that work.

- Bob

the only way that can happen is if the posterior is improper. Warning
users that they've specified an improper posterior is a valuable

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] fixed lgamma-based crashes (from neg_binomial)
parts:
On 8/26/12 1:49 PM, Matt Hoffman wrote:
> We should probably have a check somewhere that tests if any parameter
> goes (without rejection) to +-inf on its unconstrained scale, since
> the only way that can happen is if the posterior is improper. Warning
> users that they've specified an improper posterior is a valuable
> service.

That's a very good idea and won't be hard.

It's now on the to-do list under "sampling".

I'm thinking we need to trap +inf, -inf in the
samplers, as they won't be actual samples because
of the Metropolis reject steps (though they could
still be in some cases).

I could just put it in the leapfrog() calculation.

I'm also assuming I should just stop when I hit
such a value. But then not if it's due to initialization,
because we want to allow some restarts in case we
got a bad init.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] fixed lgamma-based crashes (from neg_binomial)
parts:
I'm not sure we want to die if we ever see a +-inf. There are two cases:
1. p(|θ_i|=∞) > 0
2. p(|θ_i|=∞) = 0.
Case 1 says we've got an improper posterior, and we should die in that
case. But case 2 just says that we've done a bad job of choosing a
step size, and so our leapfrog integrator has gone bananas. That's not
necessarily a huge deal, especially in the adaptation phase, so we
shouldn't do anything drastic. We could report it, though, if it's not
much of a pain.

Agree/disagree?

Matt
